## A. PRIMARY SOURCES — verified access

### A1. Annual Report of the Light-House Board (1852–1910)
- HathiTrust record 005638012 ("Annual report of the Light-House Board of the United States to the Secretary of the Treasury for the fiscal year ended ..."), OCLC 12655542, LCCN 09035241. **102 items, ALL "Full view"** (verified via bib API https://catalog.hathitrust.org/api/volumes/full/oclc/12655542.json). Enumcron year coverage: 1852, then continuous 1871–1912 (a few later Bureau-era volumes bound in through 1918). Sample item URLs: 1852 = https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015073483268 ; 1871/72 = https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=njp.32101050591773 ; 1873/74 = https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=uc1.a0004403978
- GAP 1853–1870: not in this record. I'm inferring (standard practice, not verified item-by-item this session) that those years' reports were printed inside the Treasury "state of the finances" reports and the Congressional Serial Set; the digitized Serial Set at loc.gov (see A3) is the search venue — e.g. loc.gov item 2022690513 is the Jan. 1853 Finances report.
- IA copies: 7 Google-scan items (annualreportlig00–04statgoog, annualreportlig00–01boargoog), all open access, but ALL carry the bogus metadata year "1852" — actual years unidentified; use HathiTrust for citable year runs.

### A2. Annual Report of the Commissioner of Lighthouses (Bureau of Lighthouses, 1911–1939)
- HathiTrust record 100493969, OCLC 1779112, LCCN 12004661. **11 items, ALL Full view**; coverage 1911–1932 (incl. a bound "1911-20" Harvard set: https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=hvd.hn4jj9 ; 1922 = https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=cub.u183018238366). LOC MARC note: "Continues: ... Annual report of the Light-House Board" (verified via LOC SRU lx2.loc.gov). 1933–1939 issues NOT located this session.

### A3. The 1852–53 contracts for the first eight Pacific lighthouses (Gibbons & Kelly)
Digitized Congressional Serial Set at loc.gov — four primary documents located, two downloaded and page-verified:
1. **S. Rept. 33-291** (May 29, 1854), Committee of Claims on the memorial of Gibbons & Kelly — https://www.loc.gov/item/2024887220/ ; PDF https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/ll/llserialsetpdf/00/70/7_/00/_0/0/00707_00_00/00707_00_00-108-0291-0000/SERIALSET-00707_00_00-108-0291-0000.pdf (downloaded, read). VERIFIED CONTENT: contract signed "On the 30th of April, 1852" with the Secretary of the Treasury under the acts of Sept. 28, 1850 and March 3, 1851; the Point Loma site dispute (Coast Survey's Lt. Harrison selected the point); the May 21, 1852 contract modification on tower completion; the contractors' vessel "Oriole"; freight claims for hauls to Cape Disappointment, Alcatraz ("Alcatras Island, one mile"), and Battery Point ($11,080 claimed).
2. **S. Ex. Doc. 33-53** (Feb. 17, 1855), Treasury report transmitting "all the original papers in possession of this department relating to the claim of Gibbons and Kelly" (quoted from p.1) — https://www.loc.gov/item/2025863565/ ; PDF ...SERIALSET-00752_00_00-019-0053-0000.pdf (103 MB, downloaded, p.1 verified). This is the printed correspondence file = the core primary corpus for the contract story ($59,434 claim).
3. **H. (Serial Set) doc "Gibbons and Kelly. Letter from the Secretary of the Treasury..."** (1854) — https://www.loc.gov/item/2022690880/ ; PDF ...SERIALSET-00727_00_00-003-0113-0000.pdf
4. **C.C. Rept. 34-29, "Francis A. Gibbons and Francis X. Kelly" (July 25, 1856)** Court of Claims report — https://www.loc.gov/item/2022691122/ ; PDF ...SERIALSET-00872_00_00-004-0029-0000.pdf
Also: **S. Ex. Doc. 32-28 (1852), "Report of the officers constituting the Light-house Board"** — the foundational 760-page reorganization report — https://www.loc.gov/item/2024887023/ ; PDF ...SERIALSET-00617_00_00-002-0028-0000.pdf (URL returned by loc.gov API; file not downloaded). The loc.gov Serial Set API (add ?fo=json, or /search/?q=...&fo=json) is open and is the discovery engine for CA-specific lighthouse bills (verified hits incl. "Light and fog-signal at Army Point, Suisun Bay" S. Rept. 60-773, loc.gov/item/2026562561; "Coal shed, Humboldt Bay" S. Rept. 60-747, 2026562543; "Light-ship for use on coast of California" 1901, 2024858118; "Lifesaving apparatus ... Farallone Islands" 1908, 2026561194).

## E. THE "WHY BUILT" LAYER — trade-route ties (links to the lumber-ports map's five trade lighthouses: Point Arena, Point Cabrillo, Punta Gorda, Trinidad Head, St. George Reef, per /Users/aodhan/california-history-maps/data/lumber-ports.json)
Documented, quotable evidence located in the verified NRHP nomination texts (all quotes verbatim, from the downloaded PDFs):
- **St. George Reef (93001373):** need "revealed dramatically in 1865 by the wreck of the schooner, Brother Jonathan, on the shoals of the St. George Reef with the loss of 166 lives"; May 1866 Light-House Board request → June 8, 1866 executive reservation; Jan. 1867 islets reservation; the Board-vs-Coast Survey correspondence on Northwest Seal Rock (Jan. 20, 1875 letter cited in the text). ⚠ The nomination calls Brother Jonathan a "schooner" and gives 166 lives — she is standardly identified as a sidewheel steamer; treat vessel type/casualty count as needing primary confirmation before the map states them.
- **Point Cabrillo (91001092):** "the lighthouse of the north coast lumber fleet"; "Point Cabrillo was the light of the smaller lumber schooners that served the many narrow 'doghole' ports of the Mendocino coast"; economy "totally dependent on the doghole" trade. Direct bridge to the doghole-ports layer.
- **Punta Gorda (76000483):** "From 1895 to 1907 a total of ten ships sank or went aground near Punta Gorda. The last of the ten was the Columbia, a passenger ship that collided with a lumber ship on July 12, 1907, resulting in the loss of 77 lives... in 1908, the year after the Columbia sank, Congress appropriated $60,000". ⚠ Discrepancy: the Columbia–San Pedro collision is conventionally dated July 21, 1907 with a higher death toll (~88); the existing lumber-ports map already carries the collision — reconcile against a primary wreck record before publishing either figure.
- **Trinidad Head (91001098):** Trinidad as "at one time a bustling harbor home to numerous steam schooners and sailing vessels"; "equipment, lumber, and agricultural products served to make Trinidad one of the busiest" (ports of the region).
- **Point Arena (90002189):** notes products "(lumber) were shipped out" and cites Shanks, Lighthouses and Lifeboats on the Redwood Coast, in its own bibliography — the NR record and the map's Shanks citations converge.
Primary reinforcement per station: the Annual Reports (A1) for the appropriation/recommendation year and the Light List (A4) for characteristics; Serial Set bills (A3) for harbor lights (Army Point/Suisun Bay S. Rept. 60-773 ties bay lights to river-steamer traffic). Davidson's Coast Pilot (1889) is already anchored in the lumber-ports apparatus for the trade geography.
